correctness.rationale: For nonreal z, arg(z+t) is continuous strictly monotone with derivative -Im(z)/|z+t|^2; its range has length Theta<pi. If lambda*Theta<pi, a rotation of every integrand lies in a common strict open right half-plane, so a nonzero positive integral cannot vanish. If lambda*Theta>=pi, choose two support locations separated in argument by pi/lambda and masses |z+t_i|^lambda; their integrands are antipodal unit vectors and cancel. Real admissible z>-a gives positive transform. For lambda=2, the right-angle criterion simplifies exactly to |z+(a+b)/2|^2 <= (b-a)^2/4. Independent two-atom complex arithmetic yielded residual 3.5e-15 at z=-2.7+0.35i; the constructive proof is exact.

value.rationale: The first sharp order-uniform, support-sensitive geometric answer to where positive generalized Stieltjes transforms may vanish, with an attainable region and a two-point extremal construction. Despite its elementary convex-arc proof, this is a self-contained natural complex-zero classification for a broad transform family, not an arbitrary isolated integral or routine sign check.

final_claim: For 0<=a<b, lambda>0 and nonzero positive finite measures mu on [a,b], the union over mu of zeros of S_lambda,mu(z)=integral_(a..b)(z+t)^(-lambda) dmu(t) in C\(-infty,-a] is precisely {z: |arg(z+a)-arg(z+b)| >= pi/lambda}. No zeros if lambda<=1; order 2 gives the nonreal disk with diameter [-b,-a]. Every admissible point is attained by two positive atoms.
limitations: Classifies union of attainable zero locations across positive measures, not individual transform zeros; compact interval, positive measures and principal slit branch.
